newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Korea stocks surge after Seoul rally.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Korea stocks surge after Seoul rally.

text.p: Korean global depositary receipts rose steeply in brisk trading Friday, as shares built on an eight-month high established in Seoul.
Seoul's composite index gained 1.87 percent, or 14.49 points to 789.15 points.
"The market has already anticipated an 800 point level," a trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index closed up 4.69 points, or 6.19 percent, to 80.49 points, a premium of 46.01 percent over the local market.

When enthusiasm for Korean shares spills over into the GDR market, the percentage rise is often greater, traders said, because a large percentage of GDRs are held by institutions and not actively traded.
"Whatever happens, I don't expect the premium to narrow," a trader said.
A 52-week high in the Bombay blue-chip index led to a good day in Indian GDRs Friday, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark index closed up 47.04 points, or 1.18 percent, at 4,029.99.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.35 points up at 87.99, with the premium over the local market at 28.13 percent from 27.69 percent.
Hindalco gained $1.50 to $34.25/$35.25 and Telco rose $1.57 to $15.00/$15.85.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 0.47 points, or 0.47 percent, to 122.45, representing a discount to the local market of 2.34 percent.
